subject: [mazhewitt/AgenticMailPipeline] [WIP] Refactor integration test to use phase-based concurrency, formal assertions, error aggregation, and improved maintainability (PR #1)
snippet: Thanks for asking me to work on this. I will get started on it and keep this PR's description up to date as I form a plan and make progress. Original description: Improve the integration test logic
body:
Thanks for asking me to work on this. I will get started on it and keep this PR's description up to date as I form a plan and make progress.

Original description:

> Improve the integration test logic in agentic-mail-agent/tests/integration/test_classifier_labeller_integration.rs as follows:
> 
> - Refactor the code so that within each major phase (labelling emails, verifying labels, and deleting/removing test labels), actions on individual emails or labels are performed concurrently (using proper Rust async concurrency, such as FuturesUnordered or similar patterns). However, ensure that the three phases themselves (labelling, then verifying, then deleting) are NOT run in parallel—they must happen sequentially.
> 
> - Replace as many println! debug checks as possible with assertions so that the test fails formally if expectations are not met (e.g., label presence, classification correctness, idempotency).
> 
> - Aggregate errors (such as failed label applications or verifications) and report them all at the end instead of stopping at the first failure.
> 
> - Refactor repeated logic (like label application, verification, and cleanup) into helper functions for maintainability.
> 
> - Ensure setup/teardown code reliably cleans up test labels and state even if an error or panic occurs (for example, using drop guards or similar Rust patterns).
> 
> - Where possible, reduce unnecessary Gmail API calls (such as caching label IDs when reusing labels).
> 
> - Improve error messages to include more context (such as email subject or snippet).
> 
> - Do not parallelize across the label, verify, and cleanup phases—only within each phase if safe.
> 
> - Summarize the improvements in the PR description.
